operator_scope: live camera, DESTRUCTIVE: one frame of one clip was written as compressed CinemaDNG instead of stock RAW
notes: The first attempt produced a structurally perfect but all-zero image. The cause was diagnosable from the artifact alone: ten SOI markers instead of twelve, the first at exactly the offset tile 2 would have had counting from the arena base. The codec had written at the base, and the header copy destroyed the first two tiles.

The reason was `#if OUT_OFF` against a `.equ`. A .equ is an assembler symbol and the preprocessor cannot see it, so the condition was always false. A test now asserts the built compressed image carries the offset as an immediate and the discard image does not.

finish_source compares seg[1] with the stock length, which marks every successful compressed write as ERR_SOURCE and then makes release refuse a healthy block. The check is now skipped for this phase; the header and pixel comparisons, which are what it is really for, still run.

explicitly_established.claim: the camera writes a compressed CinemaDNG to the card: 1,396,736 bytes against 3,244,544 stock, 57% smaller, and LibRaw decodes it
the writer accepts a node length different from the stock segment length; G4a had deliberately left it unchanged
the owned 79,872-byte header built on the camera is structurally correct: root IFD at 0x13400, Compression 7, tile tags present, strip tags gone, and every declared tile offset matches an actual SOI
the decoded frame matches its stock neighbour in mean and standard deviation to two decimals and differs by at most 14 LSB, which is sensor noise between consecutive frames

explicitly_not_established: losslessness OF THIS FRAME: the stock version of it no longer exists, having been replaced. The engine's bitstream was proven lossless separately, earlier the same day, on a frame whose stock copy survived
more than one frame: this is a single one-shot write, not a clip
in-camera playback, which remains impossible for tiled Compression=7
any other scene, geometry or bit depth
sustained writing, thermal behaviour, or the first-frame-derived buffer capacity across varying sizes
that the clip as a whole is well-formed: only frame 1 was replaced, and a mixed clip is not a supported thing
